genZNote: Direct-acting antivirals now cure most infections outright — a genuine good-news story next to hepatitis B, which mostly just gets suppressed.

habitat.hostAssociation: Obligate human pathogen — chronic infection in the majority of untreated cases

identificationClues: Diagnosed by anti-HCV antibody screening followed by confirmatory HCV RNA testing
Chronic infection develops in a majority of untreated cases, often without early symptoms
Genotype testing guides direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy selection

clinicalImportance.transmission: Bloodborne — injection drug use (needle sharing), less commonly sexual contact, and perinatal transmission; historically transfusion-associated before blood supply screening
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: A major cause of chronic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma worldwide; direct-acting antivirals now achieve cure rates exceeding 95% in most patients
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Anti-HCV antibody testing indicates exposure but not necessarily active infection — confirmatory HCV RNA (PCR) testing is required to diagnose current infection

examFacts.importantDisease: Chronic hepatitis C, cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma
examFacts.importantTest: Anti-HCV antibody screening confirmed by HCV RNA PCR
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Highly effective direct-acting antivirals now cure the large majority of infections, unlike hepatitis B, which is typically only suppressed
